From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted fit assessment — latency & SLO sync (Evergreen AI)

Jamie — great call earlier, thanks for the time. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment on scope for the hosted POC. TL;DR: we need to validate p95/p99 E2E latency under your realistic traffic mix (including streaming sessions) and agree acceptance thresholds before scheduling the demo/benchmark run.

What we captured on the call
- Current provider (incumbent) measurements you shared: p95 ~240 ms, p99 ~1200 ms (these are end-to-end with your front-end + network).
- Evergreen target: you mentioned wanting p95 under 200 ms and p99 under 800 ms for production.
- Traffic profile: peak concurrent requests ~250 RPS (bursty), average sustained ~120 RPS. Streaming sessions (chat assistant) peak concurrent streams ~40, average ~18.
- Payloads: typical prompt length ~120 tokens, few heavy prompts (up to 1k tokens) for long-form summarization.

What we need from you to scope the POC
1) Confirm the representative traffic file (we'll use it for traffic shaping & load generation). Please send the anonymized request sample/trace you mentioned.
2) Confirm acceptance criteria: please confirm whether p95<=200ms / p99<=800ms is the right bar, or if you prefer stricter numbers. Also confirm whether those targets apply to streaming tail latency (time-to-first-token) or only complete-response latency.
3) Peak concurrency window to emulate (we propose a 10-minute surge window at 250 RPS for acceptance).
4) Any regulatory/ingress constraints (VPC, IP allowlist) we must account for during the POC.

Our proposed POC plan
- Redwood hosted environment: we will provision a POC stack that mirrors the production serving path (same runtime, streaming enabled).
- Test harness: continuous-burst load generation + token-level tracing; we'll run baseline (no-cache) and warmed-KV-cache runs.
- Acceptance runs: two 30-minute runs — 1) 120 RPS sustained with 10-min 250 RPS surge; 2) streaming-heavy run with 40 concurrent streams. We'll report p50/p95/p99 and throughput.
- Timeline: if Evergreen can provide traffic file and confirm acceptance numbers by Fri 24 Jul, we can spin up POC infra and target week of 2 Aug for live runs.

Attachments: evergreen_slo_matrix.xlsx (proposed SLO matrix & pass/fail criteria), evergreen_traffic_profile_v1.json (empty placeholder — please replace with your sample traces).

Asks / next steps
- Jamie: share the anonymized traffic sample and confirm acceptance thresholds (p95/p99 numbers + streaming TTF).
- Procurement: if POC moves forward, please confirm required PO/NDAs we should expect.
- Ben / Hannah: can you pre-allocate a POC pool (small+medium GPU mix) and a baseline costing estimate for a 2-week POC?

Thanks — Priya

--
Priya Natarajan
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0194

Thanks Priya — thanks for the thorough summary. Confirming a few items from our side:

- Incumbent numbers: our on-prod telemetry (front-end + network + model endpoint) averages: p95 ~240ms, p99 ~1.2s. We saw occasional p99 spikes to ~1.6s during end-of-day batch jobs.
- Acceptance targets: Evergreen prefers p95 <= 200ms and p99 <= 800ms for interactive assistant endpoints. For streaming, our primary concern is time-to-first-token (TTFT) — we'd like TTFT <= 120ms and stable per-token latency so clients don't see stalls. Full-response p99 requirement applies to non-streaming batch endpoint only.
- Traffic: peak sustained bursts we want you to emulate are 10-minute windows at ~250 RPS; overall average ~120 RPS. Concurrent streaming sessions: peak 40, baseline 18.

I attached an anonymized sample traffic file (replaced user content) — evergreen_traffic_profile_v1.json. It has the mix of short chat prompts, medium completion prompts, and a few long-form requests. Use it as the canonical generator.

Procurement is on copy — we'll need a short SOW/PO for the POC (2-week), and a standard NDA. Procurement, can you confirm preferred SOW template and if DocuSign is required?

We'll tentatively hold week of Aug 2 for the runs. If Redwood can confirm infra sizing and a rough cost estimate for the demo run, we'll lock calendar and get procurement moving.

—Jamie

Internal checklist and technical notes for the POC (high level):

1) Infra sizing (initial)
- Small-GPU: 2 nodes (for streaming, lower mem models) — target 40 concurrent streams across pool.
- Medium-GPU: 3 nodes (for completions) — should handle 250 RPS burst when autoscaled across instances.
- Fallback quantized pool: 2 small nodes running int8 variant to validate graceful degradation.

2) Test harness components
- Load generator: replay evergreen_traffic_profile_v1.json with realistic inter-arrival times + configurable surge windows; measure per-request wall time (client->client).
- KV cache warmup: run a 15 minute warmup sequence with top 500 prefixes to reflect production cache hit rates.
- Streaming runs: measure time-to-first-token (TTFT) and per-token delta (ensure no token stalls >200ms).
- Telemetry: capture p50/p95/p99, tail percentiles, CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth, and request drop counts.

3) Acceptance criteria extraction
- We'll produce a single CSV per run with columns: timestamp, request_id, latency_client_ms, ttft_ms, model_tokens, cache_hit. We'll compute p95/p99 from latency_client_ms.

4) Risks / notes
- Network egress and front-end CDN behavior can add variance compared to Redwood internal numbers. Recommend Evergreen run a 'golden' synthetic client (from their network) during acceptance runs to verify network path parity.

5) Estimate (ballpark for planning)
- Infra + run time (2 weeks POC, including 2 days dry runs + 2 acceptance runs): ~$9k - $14k (depends on medium GPU hours and egress). Final quote after exact sizing.

I'll spin up the evg-poc-2026-07 label and upload the preliminary runbook to the shared drive: https://drive.redwood.company/s/evergreen-poc-runbook

Ben

Thanks — this all looks good from our side. A couple of clarifications before we lock the week of Aug 2: 

- Fallback behavior: yes, we want to validate graceful degradation. If medium-gpu pool is saturated, we expect an automatic fallback to the quantized small-gpu variant with clear performance tradeoffs. Please include fallback detection metrics in the report.
- SLA / commit ask: for production we will ask for an SLA mapping (p99 windows) and an optional credit schedule if p99 > agreed threshold over a rolling 30-day window. For the POC, a best-effort report is fine — we'll discuss SLA in commercial terms later.
- Cost: the ballpark is reasonable. Procurement, please confirm if that range is acceptable for a paid POC; we can route a short PO.

We can confirm Aug 2 as the start date for the acceptance runs once Redwood shares the final infra estimate and a short SOW (1 page). Also: Priya — can you include a suggested list of test clients we should run from our side to remove network variance?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Jamie
